quote: # Program design — rule system v1, core (issue #130, slice A)
claim: Documented-standards axis fails: one fatal breach (S1-F1, a new docs/design/ level that becomes a second owner of contract decisions) plus two advisories (S1-F2 a stale contract sentence, S1-F3 two lifecycle rows with no implementation and no recorded deferral). The rest of the S1 corpus is honoured: src/cortex/rules/constants.py reproduces the spec's calibration table value for value (PRIOR 0.5; LR 20/20/3/1/1; promote 0.9, demote 0.7, archive 0.3; 3 positive uses, 2 distinct sessions; CONTEXT_BUDGET 40; 6-month window as timedelta(days=183)) and migrations/008_rules.sql carries the spec's rules and rule_uses columns plus the two documented indexes.
premise: S1 is judged against AGENTS.md (docs/specs/rule-system.md is the single source of truth and must be updated whenever the rule system changes; domain docs follow docs/agents/domain.md) and CONTEXT.md ## Rules (Rule, Rule confidence, Staging, Split, Merge, Use attribution, Feedback classifier, Rule declaration). Corpus: git diff ecb8d6b..0df8e19, HEAD 0df8e19, working tree clean at review time.

quote: ## Deviations from the spec, decided here
claim: This commit introduces a fifth documentation level, docs/design/, and puts the PR's contract decisions in it. The documented layout has four levels with one owner each, so the file becomes a second home for decisions the spec and the ADR already own: its deviation 1 ends with 'The spec is updated in the same PR' and deviation 4 with 'noted in the spec', i.e. the same decisions are now recorded twice, in a document no level in docs/agents/domain.md owns.
premise: docs/agents/domain.md (reached from AGENTS.md 'Domain docs') states 'One owner per level; never duplicate one level's content in another' and lays out docs/ with exactly adr/, specs/, research/ and agents/; docs/design/ is the first new docs subdirectory added after that standard, and the file reproduces spec-owned material (type signatures, data model, lifecycle contracts) next to a 'Deviations from the spec' section. Cure options, both cheap: fold the content into docs/specs/rule-system.md (updated in place) or extend the documented layout in docs/agents/domain.md in the same commit. Mitigation for the parent: the repo already carries pre-standard top-level markdown (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md), so the breach is structural, not unprecedented.

quote: today carries three dimensions — facts, personality, ambient — and is
claim: The contract still asserts that MemoryContext 'today carries three dimensions' although this same diff makes rules the fourth (MemoryContext.rules plus the ContextProvider fourth dimension), so the sentence the AGENTS.md update rule requires to be kept in sync is now false inside the spec itself.

The diff adds src/cortex/agentic/models.py:112 'rules: list[Rule] = field(default_factory=list)' and src/cortex/memory/context_provider.py:84 'bundle.rules = await self.get_rules_context()', and updates the very next bullet — so the paragraph was edited without rewriting the stale clause. quote: | Manual edit | a new dictated rule replaces the old one; the old is archived and **does not inherit** its history — the evidence was about a different text |
claim: Two lifecycle-table rows are unimplemented and unaccounted. 'Manual edit' has no code path: create_dictated inserts the new rule and its dictation use and archives nothing, so the replaced rule stays active and contradicts the new one. The promotion row's tail, 'Cortex notifies with one line' (line 120), is also absent: next_state/list_active promote silently. Neither row appears in the deferred work lists.
premise: RuleService.create_dictated (src/cortex/rules/service.py:49-73) performs exactly repository.create + repository.add_use; no lookup of an existing rule with the same condition and no refresh of a predecessor. Promotion is applied inside next_state (src/cortex/rules/scoring.py:79-87) and persisted by list_active (service.py:144-152) with no notification hook. Deferral is only legitimate when the contract says so: the spec status block names only the classifier as missing, and docs/design/rule-system-core.md:3-7 lists slice A as create/record use/promote/demote/archive/split/merge and slice B as classifier/attribution/proposals/conflict check/eval fixtures — manual edit and notification are in neither list.

claim: All six ADR-0020 decisions hold. (1) Dictation is evidence and the rule starts definitive: create_dictated writes one APPROVAL use and computes posterior(PRIOR, [dictation]) ~= 0.952 with state DEFINITIVE (service.py:58, 63-73). (2) Recompute, not accumulate: record_use re-reads list_uses and recomputes from the prior (service.py:115-119). (3) Silence scores 0: DIRECTION[NEUTRAL] = 0 with LR[NEUTRAL] = 1, so a neutral use cannot move the logit (constants.py:21, 32; pinned by test_scoring.py::TestPosterior.test_neutral_use_moves_nothing). (4) Split replaces and redistributes: each use is moved to its assigned child and the parent is archived with superseded_by = first child (service.py:230-239). (5) Merge is definitive only if every parent was (service.py:268-272) and takes the union of the parents' uses (service.py:258-260, 279-283). (6) Archived is never applied: render_rules drops ARCHIVED (render.py:26) and list_active queries staging+definitive only and skips a rule archived mid-sweep (service.py:134-155).
premise: Each ADR-0020 claim was traced to code and to a witness test; the ADR's 'silence is worth zero on purpose' is the one most easily broken by a plausible implementation, and the constant plus the witness test make it explicit.

claim: Repo conventions are followed. Persistence is an ABC in interfaces.py with the Postgres implementation in repository.py (repository.py:21), and the asyncpg row mapping copies src/cortex/memory/repository.py's _row_to_fact style (_row_to_rule / _row_to_use, repository.py:153-177, enum columns decoded through RuleState()/RuleOrigin()/UseOutcome() so no bare str leaks). The CLI keeps the typer convention: --db-url option, nested async runner, asyncio.run (cli.py:160-193 for rules:list, 196-247 for rules:show, 250-281 for rules:archive), matching token:create and traces:cleanup. The package __init__ re-exports models, interfaces and implementations exactly like cortex.trace and cortex.sessions. main.py wires PostgresRuleRepository + RuleService in the composition root and injects it into ContextProvider (main.py:182-187, 230-235). Tests live in tests/unit/rules/ with fakes.py and a mocked-session repository test, mirroring tests/unit/trace/.
premise: Baseline files read for comparison: src/cortex/memory/repository.py, src/cortex/trace/repository.py, src/cortex/sessions/, src/cortex/cli.py (token:create, traces:cleanup), src/cortex/main.py, tests/unit/trace/{fakes.py,test_trace_repository.py}. One deliberate, documented divergence, not filed as a finding: PostgresRuleRepository takes an injectable session_factory defaulting to DbSession (repository.py:30-33) where the other Postgres repositories call DbSession() directly, and its tests inject a factory instead of patching cortex.*.repository.DbSession; the class docstring justifies it (the CLI's own --db-url connection) and production behaviour is identical.

claim: Fowler baseline: no smell reaches the documented-standard bar, so the item passes with six labelled advisories (S4-F1..S4-F6). Found: duplicated code (S4-F1 the CLI runner scaffold, S4-F6 the 0.5 prior), long function (S4-F2 split), data clumps / long parameter list (S4-F3 record_use), speculative generality (S4-F4 the deleted session_id, S4-F5 'two or more' children). Not found: large class (RuleService is eight cohesive lifecycle methods over 307 lines), divergent change, shotgun surgery, feature envy, primitive obsession beyond the rule text the spec deliberately leaves open ('The shape of a rule's text ... a choice, not a decision'), switch statements (outcome dispatch is the two constant dicts quoted here, not an if-ladder over outcomes), temporary field.
premise: Fowler smells are judgements: advisory unless they breach a documented repo standard, which none of these does. Thresholds applied: long function > ~50 lines; long parameter list > 3 parameters that always travel together; duplicated code = the same statement block with the same shape in 3+ places. Line counts measured on HEAD 0df8e19 (src/cortex/rules/service.py 307 lines, src/cortex/cli.py 294 lines).

claim: Duplicated code: the three rules commands start from the same scaffold — asyncpg.connect(_database_url(db_url)), PostgresRuleRepository(session_factory=lambda: _AsyncpgRuleSession(conn)), then a try whose finally closes the connection — beginning at cli.py:175, 213 and 267. One async context manager yielding the repository would leave each command with only its own work.
premise: Three occurrences of the identical statement sequence, differing only in the service call between them; token:create and traces:cleanup already carry their own inline copies, so the pattern is spreading rather than contained.

claim: Long function: RuleService.split spans service.py:172-240 (69 lines) and merge spans 242-293 (52 lines). split mixes assignment validation (197-209), child creation (211-228), use redistribution (230-234) and parent retirement (236-239), each a separable step with its own failure mode; the docstring already enumerates them as four responsibilities.
premise: Measured on HEAD 0df8e19; ~50 lines is the usual long-method band and the repo sets no mechanical limit (pyproject enables no C901), so this is advisory. The validation-before-write invariant (a rejected split leaves no child behind) is what keeps the four steps in one function today.

claim: Data clump / long parameter list: record_use takes (rule_id, session_id, situation, outcome) — exactly the fields of RuleUse minus occurred_at (models.py:78-86) — and immediately rebuilds that dataclass inside add_use (service.py:106-114). Passing a RuleUse would carry the same information as one typed value instead of four positional scalars, two of them bare UUIDs.
premise: Four parameters that always travel together and are already declared together in models.py; the two UUID parameters are the primitive-obsession edge of the same smell (a rule_id and a session_id are interchangeable at the call site). Advisory: the service owns occurred_at, so a partial RuleUse would be needed.

claim: Speculative generality: create_from_correction accepts a session_id and immediately deletes it, justified only by 'symmetry with create_dictated'. A parameter the function discards is a misleading contract — the docstring itself says a correction-born rule records no evidence until it is applied, so the session has no role in this call.
premise: Nothing in the spec requires the two create methods to share an arity; docs/specs/rule-system.md ## Lifecycle distinguishes them precisely by the evidence each records. Advisory because a slice-B classifier call site may plausibly invoke both with the same tuple.

quote: """Replace a rule with two or more complementary ones.
claim: Speculative generality: split is widened from the glossary's Split (one rule replaced by TWO complementary rules) to 'two or more', guarded by len(children) < 2 (line 186) and returning list[Rule]. No spec text, ADR text or test exercises three children, and the extra generality makes the two-child contract implicit: 'child 0 inherits the parent's state' (line 221) is a positional convention the widened signature no longer states.
premise: CONTEXT.md **Split**: 'The replacement of one Rule by two complementary Rules with disjoint conditions'; docs/specs/rule-system.md ## Split repeats 'two rules'. Advisory, not fatal: a superset API does not contradict the two-rule case, but it is untested generality (tests/unit/rules/test_service.py only ever splits into two).

claim: Duplicated code around a documented single-source constant: the 0.5 prior and the staging default live in three places — constants.py:13 (PRIOR = 0.5) plus models.py:60-61 (state: RuleState = RuleState.STAGING, confidence: float = 0.5) plus migrations/008_rules.sql:13-14 (DEFAULT 'staging', DEFAULT 0.5). constants.py opens by claiming to be the single home ('the only magic numbers in it') and the spec agrees ('These are the only magic numbers in the system'), so a calibration change now means editing three files and the two silent copies fail quietly if one is missed.
premise: Duplicated-code smell on a constant the spec calls isolated and documented. No current behaviour is wrong — RuleService always sets confidence (create_dictated via posterior(...), create_from_correction passes PRIOR explicitly) and the state (both create paths) — the risk is divergence between the Python default and the SQL default of rows written outside the service.

claim: No user data reaches SQL through interpolation. All six f-string statements interpolate only the module-level constant column tuples _RULE_COLUMNS (repository.py:14-17) and _USE_COLUMNS (line 18); every value — id, condition, action, rationale, the state/origin/outcome strings, timestamps, the state list and the use-id list — is bound as a $n parameter (e.g. lines 45-54, 110-111, 146-149). The user-controlled free text (condition, action, rationale, situation) therefore only ever appears as a bound parameter.
premise: S7 risk: f-string SQL must interpolate constant column lists only, never user data. Interpolation sites enumerated: repository.py:38-44, 61, 71-76, 88-93, 103-109, 124-130 (five triple-quoted plus one inline), each over the two constant tuples and nothing else; reassign_uses (line 146) and every other statement use placeholders only, and cli.py issues no SQL of its own (it goes through the repository).
